##  · R2-image-fields — Startup block image fields for the loader stub

Status: **resolved** · Assigned to: Orchestrator · Revision: 9

*Resolved in an earlier workspace; reopen it if the code has changed since.*

Decision references: docs/archive/2026-09-22/QUESTIONS.md: 65 (answered), docs/INIT.md: Startup block (startup opcode 1, image_addr/image_len), docs/PACKAGES.md: Launching a process, step 4

Evidence: Image fields defined in the startup table and implemented in libs/wire/src/proto/startup.rs (regenerated with redoubt-wire-gen, --check clean, c8efafa14) and read by stub read_image. R2 host side passed red-team round 3 at wp-r2 47cf82c1c. Remaining R2 work is tracked in R2-after-K5a.

### Implementer · Question

Event: `622a5adf7a436bd7bac8701bf93709e6` · 2026-09-24T07:03:08Z

> R2 (loader stub) needs two new fields on INIT.md's `startup` wire table so the stub (running inside the child) can find the ELF image its parent copied in (PACKAGES.md, Launching a process, step 4; BUILD-PLAN WP-R2).
> 
> Recommendation: add to the `startup` message (opcode 1), after `argv`:
> - `image_addr: u64` — the first byte of the ELF image, which the parent mapped read-write into the child's own address space (`process_map`), page-aligned. 0 means "no image named" (a process started directly at its own entry, not through the stub — e.g. the boot bundle's initial processes, or a launcher that already knows its child's entry).
> - `image_len: u64` — the exact byte length of the image (not rounded to pages); bytes in the image's last page past this length are not part of it. Must be 0 iff `image_addr` is 0.
> 
> Why `u64` for both, not `u32`: WIRE.md's convention for addresses/lengths that must be the same shape on both widths (cf. `read`'s `block: u64` in the example table); an rv64 address does not fit `u32`.
> 
> Why paired presence rather than a separate boolean: mirrors `handle_count`/`handles` and keeps the block one shape for every process, stub-launched or not; `redoubt-rt`'s startup reader treats `(0, 0)` as "no image" and anything else as a candidate the stub validates (page-aligned `image_addr`, `image_addr + image_len` does not overflow). It cannot check the range lies inside what the parent actually mapped — a parent that lies can only fault its own child (PACKAGES.md, "A malicious ELF can at most compromise the process it was going to become").
> 
> Separately, and not blocking this question: PACKAGES.md says the stub is mapped "at a fixed address, the same for everyone." I plan to treat that address as an implementation constant in a small shared crate both the stub and its launchers (`init`, the steward) import, not a spec table entry, since `process_map`'s destination address is caller-chosen (KERNEL-SPEC.md) and nothing else needs to know the value. Flag if you'd rather this live in INIT.md instead.
> 
> Please add `image_addr`/`image_len` to INIT.md's `startup` table (or tell me if you want a different shape) so I can regenerate the wire codec and migrate `redoubt-rt`'s startup reader/writer.

### Architect · Answer

Event: `02b9bd6acaa8b194c65501bbf87fa828` · 2026-09-24T07:06:21Z

> Accepted as you proposed, and applied (unstaged, docs only). No new owner approval was needed: answer 65 (archive/2026-09-22) already approved "the image is named in the startup block, pointing at pages the parent mapped; R2 defines it". This just fills in the fields.
> 
> Changes:
> - docs/INIT.md, Startup block: the `startup` table (opcode 1) now reads `version: u32, handle_count: u32, namespace: bytes, handles: bytes, argv: bytes, image_addr: u64, image_len: u64`. There is a new bullet defining the two fields: page-aligned first byte in pages the parent mapped read-write; exact byte length; both 0 = no image, and the stub refuses such a block. Rules added: image_addr is 0 exactly when image_len is 0; image_addr is page-aligned; image_addr + image_len does not overflow; a lying parent faults only its own child. The intro sentence now names the fields.
> - docs/PACKAGES.md, Launching step 4: points at the INIT fields and drops the "defined with the stub" placeholder.
> - `version` stays 1. The layout has never been released, and WP-R2 migrates every writer and reader together. A mismatched pair already fails decoding and is refused whole. Please do migrate everything in one change: redoubt-wire regen, the redoubt-rt reader/writer, init, and any bench or test block writers.
> 
> Stub address: agreed, it's an implementation constant in one shared crate, not a spec table entry. The stub is mapped with process_map before start, so its range is occupied, and no kernel-chosen address in the child can land on it. Constraint: keep it inside the userspace region on both widths (below 0x8000_0000, clear of DEFAULT_HEAP_BASE 0x2000_0000 and the stack top; MEMORY-LAYOUT.md). Tell me the value when you fix it, and I'll add one line to MEMORY-LAYOUT's userspace regions.
> 
> Please check before you build on it: KERNEL-SPEC R11 says the kernel chooses the addresses map_anon returns, "nothing may depend on them". process_map is refused once the process has started. So the stub, running inside the started child, cannot place segments at an ELF's fixed p_vaddr. Under the current spec that means position-independent images (static-pie) that the stub relocates. If you need fixed-address segments instead, that is a KERNEL-SPEC change and needs an owner decision, so raise it on this thread before implementing. Question 134 (shared image pages) stays open and does not change this.
> 
> Returning the thread to you; the orchestrator or R2's reviewer resolves it once the codec migration lands.

### Implementer · Answer

Event: `9170fa27a5e4566155a88d9bacfe1f79` · 2026-09-24T07:17:05Z

> Thanks -- accepted, and I've asked the orchestrator to sync docs/INIT.md and docs/PACKAGES.md into my worktree so I can regenerate the codec and migrate redoubt-rt/init/bench block writers in one change, as instructed.
> 
> On the fixed-address-vs-PIE question you raised: I found the same gap independently while starting the stub's mapping code (before seeing your answer) and opened a dedicated thread, `R2-stub-self-map`, with the full writeup -- the exact same conclusion (`map_anon`'s address is kernel-chosen, `process_map` refuses a started process, so nothing today lets the stub place a segment at its own fixed `p_vaddr`). Rather than duplicate the analysis here: could you answer on that thread? My recommendation there is fixed-address segments via a new syscall (e.g. `map_fixed(addr, len, flags)`, same admission/W^X rules as `map_anon`/`set_flags`), not static-PIE relocation -- every Redoubt native binary today (test-programs included) is built and linked as a fixed-address, non-relocatable static, and `spawn.rs`'s own doc comment relies on that ("identical addresses mean the copy's code... resolve as they do here"). Introducing PIE relocation just for images the stub loads would be a second linking convention alongside the one every other binary uses, and the stub would need to carry a relocation-table parser and applier that PACKAGES.md never mentions. A `map_fixed` syscall is the smaller, more consistent change and keeps "the stub needs no file access... parses the ELF from memory, maps its segments" exactly as written.
